sourceRepository.confidence: repository-source snapshot; deployment to a particular PTR realm not verified

findings.confidence: high for described implementation at inspected commit; realm deployment unverified
details: Server active specialization is stored in character setting core.ascension_active_spec.
Catalog data comes from client CharacterAdvancement.dbc and ChrSpecs.dbc.
Server derives learned talent rank from character_spell; it does not maintain a separate talent table.
Specialization-to-tab matching uses internal token from ChrSpecs field 2 joined to class token and CharacterAdvancement tab token. Display name is a separate field and must not be used as join key.
Client C_CharacterAdvancement.GetActiveChrSpec resolves specialization from held identity entries; server sends active slot index/capacity separately.

findings.confidence: high for documented protocol; validate exact current client build before addon assumptions
details: SMSG 0x0725 contains active specialization slot index and slot count. CoA classes are documented as receiving capacity 20.
SMSG 0x0726 carries complete known-entry state and follows initial state, uploads, resets, specialization switches, and level changes.
ASCENSION_CA_SPECIALIZATION_ACTIVE_ID_CHANGED is a shipped client event registered by the UI; event handler should refresh by querying C_CharacterAdvancement.GetActiveChrSpec.
Inspect uses CMSG 0x06E1 and SMSG 0x06E2; server can return active slot and known entries.

findings.confidence: medium until class/spec and spell catalog joins are built
details: Repository documents Warcraft Reborn stock-spell twins: custom Reborn spell IDs may be stock spell ID + 1,100,000.
A Details parser keyed only to stock spell IDs may miss custom Reborn spell events; normalize with explicit alias rows only when name/effect identity is supported.

findings.confidence: high for source behavior in repository snapshot; deployment and runtime logs unverified
details: TinkerState tracks summons in a set of ObjectGuid values.
Source declares Owner(Unit const*), Owned(Player*,Unit*), PetCast, Summon, DeviceEvent, and device/summon lifecycle helpers.
This is promising server evidence for owner attribution and summon lifetime; it does not itself prove what combat-log source flags the client receives.
The targeted search establishes class-advancement infrastructure and one Tinker-specific ownership API.
A complete class-by-class spell/summon mapping still requires a systematic pass over CharacterAdvancement DBC/SQL migrations and src/server/coa class scripts.
Code in public main is not proof that a PTR realm deployed it or that a live character uses the behavior.

implementationGuidance: Use runtime client APIs as first choice for the player’s active class/spec; query after specialization-change event.
Maintain both displayName and internal spec token in the Details class/spec registry.
Store spell aliases as explicit normalized relationships with provenance; do not blindly add 1,100,000 to arbitrary spell IDs.
For pets, track owner GUID separately from unit GUID and preserve unknown attribution when an event arrives before owner association.
Keep repository-derived evidence separate from live combat-log-observed evidence.
